subject: Hosted API commit uplift — execution plan & quota recast
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Cole <erin@shoply.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit uplift — execution plan & quota recast

Hi Erin — great to see Shoply's Q1 usage. Per our call last week I put together a compact plan to move you from the current monthly commit to the higher tier we discussed so you get predictable throughput and a larger burst pocket during peak checkout events.

Summary (proposal):
- New monthly commit: 12M tokens (up from 6M)
- Rate band: move from Tier B (200rps cap) to Tier C (400rps cap)
- Burst pocket: 2M tokens per month, configurable to daily peaks
- Implementation window: 2-week rollout after signed SOW

Operational items for on-boarding:
1) Confirm final commit and invoicing cadence
2) DocuSign SOW + PO from Shoply finance
3) Provide example traffic pattern (hourly) for autoscale tuning
4) Assign an ops contact for cutover (we can do canary + full flip)

I've attached the Q1 usage report and our updated pricing matrix. If you want, I can loop in Karthik for any special SLA/latency guarantees and Neha for billing cadence.

Next step: suggest a 30-min handoff call with Ops and your engineering lead this week. Are you available Wed or Thu?

Thanks —
Jasmine
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: shoply_usage_q1.csv, redwood_pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx
From: Erin Cole <erin@shoply.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Shoply Ops <ops@shoply.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uplift — execution plan & quota recast

Thanks Jasmine — this looks sensible and aligns with our projections. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I pull procurement in: 

1) Will the rate band change require any client-side changes (we currently hard-limit at 250rps to stay in Tier B)?
2) If we exceed the monthly commit during a big PR-driven spike, how are overages charged and do we get temporary burst forgiveness for one-off incidents?
3) Can you confirm the latency SLO for the Tier C route (p95 token latency)?

We can do Thu 4/7 at 11am PT for a handoff with our infra lead (I'll add them once I confirm). Procurement will want a DocuSign SOW and a sample invoice line for our AP team.

—Erin
Head of Product Ops, Shoply
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Cole <erin@shoply.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uplift — execution plan & quota recast

Thanks Erin — quick answers below, and looping in Karthik/Vanessa/Neha for details and legal/billing: 

1) Client changes: No code changes required for Shoply's client. The change is server-side routing and rate limit configuration. If you decide to raise client-side safety limits later that's optional.

2) Overages: Standard overage policy applies (per-token rate from pricing matrix). For one-off incident spikes we can apply a one-time courtesy buffer (up to 10% of monthly commit) on first incident — we typically negotiate this in the SOW. For ongoing overage risk we recommend converting a portion of the burst pocket into committed tokens.

3) Latency SLO: Route in Tier C will be 95% of model tokens served under 180ms p95 on our hosted runtime in us-west-2 (for the vetted model variant). We'll include a fallback route to the lower-cost model variant to preserve availability if capacity is constrained.

Karthik — can you confirm if the SOW needs a specific clause for the courtesy buffer and the fallback routing language? Neha — I'll need a sample invoice line and preferred billing cadence to attach to the SOW. Vanessa — ops playbook: is two-week rollout and canary fine?

Jasmine
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Erin Cole <erin@shoply.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uplift — execution plan & quota recast

Erin / Jasmine — confirmed on legal and SLA language. Proposed SOW additions: 
- Courtesy buffer: one-time 10% complimentary buffer for the first spike within 60 days of go-live (explicitly not recurrent).
- Fallback routing: vendor will route to compatible model variant (same checkpoint, lower-cost configuration) when primary capacity constrained; fallback may have slightly higher latency and lower max tokens per response and will be logged.
- Change control: any permanent commit changes require 30 days' written notice.

Billing line (Neha, feel free to refine): 
"Hosted API — Monthly committed tokens: 12,000,000 tokens — Rate band C (400rps) — Monthly charge: $16,800 (see pricing matrix)"

Vanessa — ops: two-week rollout with a 3-day canary window + param rollback looks safe. Also recommend we pre-warm KV caches for Shoply's 3 most common prompt prefixes (Jasmine: can you ask Erin to share the top 3 prompt prefixes?).

Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Erin Cole <erin@shoply.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Shoply Ops <ops@shoply.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uplift — execution plan & quota recast

Thanks everyone — that covers our questions. Confirming:
- We approve the 12M monthly commit and Tier C rate band.
- Procurement will send PO EOD Mon 4/11 and sign DocuSign SOW (please send the final SOW including the buffer and fallback clauses).
- Ops call scheduled Thu 4/14 11am PT — I'll add our infra lead and a procurement observer.

Jasmine — I'll forward the top 3 prompt prefixes and a sample traffic CSV before EOD tomorrow so you can pre-warm caches.

—Erin
Head of Product Ops, Shoply
Attachments mentioned: SOW_shoply_hosted_uplift_draft.pdf
